header.userPrompt:
Implement https://github.com/VirtusLab/orca/issues/192 (find a recorded session by branch in `orca continue`) using the design below. It replaces the issue's proposal: there is NO separate run label (`--name`); the branch is the label. The issue text is partly stale — trust this design and the current code.

Background facts (verified against the code):
- `RunManifest` is now `AttemptManifest` (runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/manifest/AttemptManifest.scala), one per attempt. No golden fixture exists; no on-disk compatibility is owed for manifests. An absent `Option` field decodes as `None` under `JsonData.strictCodecConfig`.
- `--skip-branch` runs do bind a branch (`BranchMode.Reused`, the user's current branch) — record it too.
- The branch is bound in `FlowLifecycle.setup` (`session.bindBranch`), after `AttemptManifestWriter.start` in `flowEntry.scala`. `createFreshBranch` may fall back to `flow-<hash>`, so the bound branch (not the derived name) must be recorded.
- No structured event carries the branch today.

## Part 1 — record, group, show, select

1. Record:
   - Add `OrcaEvent.BranchBound(branch: String)` (tools/src/main/scala/orca/events/OrcaEvent.scala). Emit it once in `FlowLifecycle.setup` right after `bindBranch` returns, covering fresh, corrupt-log, resume, Created and Reused arms.
   - `LoggingListener` and `TerminalEventListener` match exhaustively: add a case (the terminal one ignores it — a Step already announces the branch; the logging one may log it).
   - `AttemptManifest.branch: Option[String]`; a pure `ManifestState.withBranch` step; the writer handles the event with `safeWrite()`. No new mutable state (the existing actor-held state only).
2. Group: add the attempt's branch to `SessionPicker.lineageKey` → `(workDir, branch, agent, minted)`. Today every run's `implementer` in one checkout collapses into one lineage and older runs hide behind "show N earlier occurrences"; with the branch in the key each run gets its own primary row, while resumed attempts of one run (same branch) still group.
3. Show:
   - Picker rows (primary, earlier, ephemeral labels): append ` on <branch>` when recorded.
   - `@<dir>` tag (`SessionPicker.dirTag`): a worktree's directory is a 12-hex RunKey, so it is noise when a branch is shown. Show `@<dir>` only for rows with no branch, or when two rows would show the same branch from different working directories.
   - `orca continue --list`: a `branch` column; `--json`: `branch` field (`Tables.SessionRow`, null when absent).
   - `SessionAction.identityNotice` (pre-resume notice): include the branch, and warn when the working directory's current branch differs from the recorded one (resume still proceeds).
   - The shell's "Resume interrupted run" menu item (`ResumeDetector`/`InterruptedRun`, `MainMenu.resumeLabel`): show the progress header's `branch`.
4. Select (`SessionPicker.resolveSelection`):
   - All-digits selector → index (unchanged).
   - Otherwise match exactly on session name (today) and on branch.
   - Only branch matches → newest durable lineage among attempts on that branch; refuse when the matches span more than one working directory, like `selectByName` does.
   - Both kinds match → refuse, naming both, pointing at `orca continue --list`. No precedence order.
   - No match → today's error plus a "did you mean" listing recorded branches that contain the selector as a substring. Never auto-pick.

## Part 2 — `--branch <name>` for runs that create a branch

- Headless: `orca run <flow> --branch <name> [task]`, parsed by the shell CLI and by `OrcaArgs` (flow-script argv). Keep it as `OrcaArgs.branch: Option[...]` (a small domain type, not a raw String in the model); do NOT move it into `RunTarget`'s cases. Refuse `--skip-branch --branch` in the shared decision alongside the existing `--worktree` refusals. Render it back in the shell's relaunch argv (next to `RunTarget.toArgv`) so shell relaunches keep it.
- Validate at parse time against git's real rules (`git check-ref-format --branch <name>` semantics — reject `:`, `~`, `^`, `@{`, `..`, trailing `.`/`.lock`, etc.) and against protected branches (`FeatureBranch`/`RecoveryCheck`). `RecoveryCheck.isSafeReusedRef` alone is too weak.
- `FlowLifecycle.freshRun`: a given name wins over the flow's `BranchNamingStrategy` and the default. No fallback on collision: an existing branch refuses with a clear message (check out the branch and use `--skip-branch`, or pick another name).
- Resume (progress log found): the header's branch is authoritative. `--branch` equal to it is fine; different → refuse.
- `--worktree`: works unchanged — the worktree path stays keyed by RunKey; the feature branch is created on top of `orca-worktree-<hash>` inside it.
- Interactive shell (`Main.runFlow`): after `promptRunTarget`, when the target creates a branch, one text prompt "Branch name (Enter to derive from the task):", validated with the same function, re-asking on an invalid name.

## Tests

Targeted, one scenario each: writer records `BranchBound`; setup emits it on fresh/resume/skip-branch; `--branch` wins over a strategy; collision refuses; resume mismatch refuses; parse + `--skip-branch --branch` refusal + argv round-trip; invalid ref refused at parse; lineages split by branch; branch selection, both-kinds refusal, cross-workdir refusal, did-you-mean; labels show the branch and worktree rows drop `@hash`; `--list` column and `--json` field; identity-notice mismatch warning.

## Docs

README command table and `run`/`continue` help (document the digits-are-an-index rule), `skills/using-orca/SKILL.md` (`--branch`, `continue <branch>`), and AGENTS.md where the manifest/picker is described.

resultJson.description:
Make the git branch a run binds to a first-class, recorded label so `orca continue` can find a session by branch (GitHub issue VirtusLab/orca#192), and let a user choose that branch up front with `orca run --branch <name>`. There is no separate run label: the branch IS the label.

Today the branch is decided in `FlowLifecycle.setup` and written only to the progress-log header. The attempt manifest the shell reads for the session picker never sees it, so every run's `implementer` session in one checkout collapses into one lineage, older runs hide behind "show N earlier occurrences", and a worktree row is tagged with a 12-hex `@<dir>` that means nothing to a person. Part 1 threads the bound branch from setup, through a new `OrcaEvent.BranchBound`, into `AttemptManifest.branch`, then uses it everywhere the shell shows or resolves a session: `continue --list`/`--json`, lineage grouping and picker labels, the pre-resume identity notice (warning when the checkout is now on a different branch), the "Resume interrupted run" menu row, and `continue <selector>` (exact branch match beside session name; refusals for ambiguity; a "did you mean" substring hint). Part 2 adds `--branch <name>` to the flow-script argv and the shell's `orca run` (validated at parse time against git's ref rules and the protected floor, refused with `--skip-branch`), makes it win over the flow's naming strategy with no fallback on collision, requires it to match the header on resume, renders it in the shell's relaunch argv, and asks for it with one text prompt in the interactive shell when the run will create a branch.

No on-disk compatibility is owed for manifests (0.x), so the manifest shape simply changes; a manifest written before this epic decodes with `branch = None` under the strict codec and renders as it does today.

In `FlowLifecycle.setup`, emit `OrcaEvent.BranchBound(binding.featureBranch.value)` immediately after `session.bindBranch(...)` returns. Add the case to `LoggingListener` (info `branch bound: {}`) and `TerminalEventListener` (ignored; comment that the git/resume Steps already announce the branch). Run `sbt "runner/testOnly orca.runner.FlowLifecycleTest"` and `sbt compile`.

tasks.title: Resolve `orca continue <selector>` by branch as well as session name

## Modules and files

- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/events/OrcaEvent.scala`: the `OrcaEvent` enum and `OrcaListener`. Exhaustive matchers that need a new case: `runner/.../runner/LoggingListener.scala` and `runner/.../runner/terminal/TerminalEventListener.scala` (`event match` at ~line 45). `AttemptManifestWriterState.onEvent`, `flow/.../events/CostTracker.scala` and `CostResolvingDispatcher.scala` end in a wildcard (verified) and compile unchanged.
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/progress/`: `FeatureBranch` (opaque; constructors `resolve` = strict slug shape, `resolveReused` = weaker shape accepting mixed case and `/`; both refuse `RecoveryCheck.alwaysProtected ∪ protectedBranches` case-insensitively and return `Left(ProtectedBranchRefused | UnsafeBranchRefRefused)`), `RecoveryCheck` (`isSafeReusedRef`, `alwaysProtected = Set("main","master")`, `validateHeader`), `ProgressLog.scala` (`ProgressHeader(startingBranch, branch, branchMode, userPrompt, flowName, startingCommit)`), `BranchMode.{Created, Reused}`. `orca.BranchNamingStrategy` in `flow/src/main/scala/orca/` (`resolve(userPrompt, agent)(using InStage): String`, `fromText`, `flowFallbackName`).
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaArgs.scala`: `RawArgs` (mainargs, one `@arg` per flag) → `OrcaArgs(userPrompt = "", verbose = false, target = NewBranch(Stash))` via `OrcaArgs.parse: Either[String, OrcaArgs]`; existing fields already carry defaults, tests build `OrcaArgs("prompt")`. `runner/src/main/scala/orca/RunTarget.scala`: `NewBranch(uncommitted) | CurrentBranch(uncommitted) | Worktree`; `RunTarget.from(worktree, skipBranch, keepChanges): Either[String, RunTarget]` is THE shared refusal decision (called by `OrcaArgs.parse` and shell `Cli.run`); `toArgv` renders flags back. Design decision: `RunTarget` gains no branch case/field.
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flowEntry.scala`: `flow()` → `runIn` starts `AttemptManifestWriter.start(...)` and passes it in `extraListeners` BEFORE `runFlow` → `runInContext` → `FlowLifecycle.setup(..., emit = dispatcher.onEvent)`, so the writer already sees setup's events.
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala`: `setup(args, agent, git, workDir, branchNaming, resolution, stackOverridden, store, sessionStore, flowName, emit, tty, ask): FlowSetup`; at ~line 378 `val binding = session.bindBranch(startBranch, protectedBranches, discovered)` returns `BranchBinding(featureBranch: FeatureBranch, startBranch, branchMode, startingCommit)`. `SetupSession.bindBranch` arms: Corrupt→`freshBinding`, Unreadable→throw, Absent→`freshBinding`, Loaded→`resumeBinding`. `freshRun(args, agent, git, workDir, branchNaming, store, startBranch, protectedBranches, discovered, flowName, headAtBinding, emit)(using InStage, WorkspaceWrite): FeatureBranch`: `if args.target.skipBranch then reuseCurrentBranch(...) else` strategy → `FeatureBranch.resolve` (protected → `flow-<hash>` fallback via `resolveFallback`) → `createFreshBranch(git, candidate, fallback, emit)` (git `Left(BranchAlreadyExists)` → retry with fallback; double collision → `OrcaFlowException`); then writes the `ProgressHeader` and `git.forceCommitOnly`. `resumeBinding(log, protectedBranches, discovered)` validates with `RecoveryCheck.validateHeader`, cross-checks `git.currentBranch() == header.branch`, then `announceResume`. `GitTool.createBranch(name)(using WorkspaceWrite): Either[BranchAlreadyExists, Unit]`; `GitTool.defaultBranch(): Option[String]` reads `origin/HEAD`.
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/manifest/`: `AttemptManifest(orcaVersion, flow, workDir, pid, startedAt, finishedAt, status, sessions)` with a jsoniter codec under `JsonData.strictCodecConfig` (an absent `Option` field decodes as `None`); `ManifestSession(harness, wireId, agent, role, stage, minted: Option[SessionKey], lastActiveAt)`. `AttemptManifestWriterState` holds `private var state: ManifestState` (actor-serialised, the sanctioned mutable state); `ManifestState(stageStack, entries, phase)` with pure steps `entered/exited/withSession/finished`; `write()` builds the manifest; every write goes through `safeWrite()`.

## Facts that would otherwise cost a re-read

- `--skip-branch` runs bind `BranchMode.Reused` with the user's current branch as the `FeatureBranch` (`reuseCurrentBranch`); it must be recorded too.
- `createFreshBranch` may return the `flow-<hash>` fallback, so the recorded branch is `binding.featureBranch.value`, never the strategy's name. Emitting once in `setup` after `bindBranch` covers every arm.
- No structured event carries the branch today; `Step("on branch '...'")`/`Step("Switched to a new branch ...")` are prose from `OsGitTool`/`announceResume`, so `TerminalEventListener` ignores the new event.
- Parse time cannot know the repo's default branch (a git query), so parse checks git ref rules plus `RecoveryCheck.alwaysProtected`; `freshRun` re-checks a user-given name against the full `protectedBranches` set with `FeatureBranch.resolveReused` (`resolve`'s slug shape would reject `feature/JIRA-123`) and refuses, with no fallback rename.
- `git check-ref-format --branch` rules: non-empty; not `HEAD`; not the single char `@`; no leading `-`; no `..`; no `@{`; no ASCII control chars, space, `~`, `^`, `:`, `?`, `*`, `[`, `\`; no `/`-component beginning with `.` or ending with `.lock`; no leading/trailing `/`, no `//`; not ending with `.`. `RecoveryCheck.isSafeReusedRef` covers only part of this.
- `--worktree` needs no change: `WorktreeRun.resolve` keys the path by `RunKey` and puts the worktree on `orca-worktree-<key>`; `freshRun` creates the feature branch on top inside it.
- `dirTag` rule after this epic: the tag is still only ever shown when the listed attempts span >1 workDir; within such a listing a row shows it only when its attempt has no recorded branch, or when its branch is shown by rows from more than one workDir. Signature becomes `(workDir: String, branch: Option[String]) => String`, so `Tables.SessionRow` needs `branch` before the picker consumes it.
- All-digits selector rule: `orca continue 123` is an index even if a branch is named `123`; use `s.forall(_.isDigit)` rather than `toIntOption` (which also accepts `+1`), and treat a digits-only string `toIntOption` rejects (overflow) as out of range.
- The exact-JSON test in `AttemptManifestWriterTest` (`a finished manifest with one durable session has this exact JSON`) pins the wire shape and must change; `manifestWithSession/manifestWithoutSessions` fixture strings carry no `branch` key and need none. `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/sessions/ManifestFixtures.manifest(...)` and `ManifestRoundTripTest` construct `AttemptManifest` directly.
- Test homes: selector/listing tests in `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/cli/CliTest.scala` (`attemptsFixture()` ~line 794 builds two attempts with `durable(sessionName = ...)`); picker/label and `runFlow` tests in `shell/.../MainTest.scala` (`FlowScriptedUi(selectScript, inputMultilineScript, inputScript, confirmScript)` with `inputCount`); `identityNotice` in `shell/.../actions/SessionActionTest.scala`; resume label in `MainMenuTest`/`ResumeDetectorTest`; `FlowLifecycle.setup` in `runner/.../FlowLifecycleTest.scala` using `GitRepo.seeded()`, `new OsGitTool(workDir)` (a non-final `private[orca]` class — override `defaultBranch()` in an anonymous subclass to simulate a detected default), `StubAgent.claude`, `ProgressStore.default(workDir, RunKey.of(prompt))`, `scratchSessions()`, and an `AtomicReference[List[OrcaEvent]]` emit sink (~line 695).

## Conventions

- Scala 3 braceless; explicit return types on public members; no class-level `var`s (the actor-held `ManifestState` is the exception — extend it with pure steps); opaque types for domain strings; `Either[String, _]` for CLI/parse refusals, `OrcaFlowException` for setup refusals; no default values on persisted fields (`AttemptManifest.branch` is a required constructor argument; test fixture helpers may default it).
- Comments are present-tense facts, no history, no plan labels; scaladoc = contract, inline `//` = why. User-facing refusals name the next action.
- Tests: munit, one scenario each, `GitRepo` temp repos and in-memory fakes only. `sbt "<module>/testOnly <Suite>"`; `sbt scalafmtAll` before finishing; zero warnings.
- Invoke the `direct-style-scala` skill before writing Scala (CLAUDE.md mandate).
